On the final day of voting, Moscow officials reported a large‑scale drone strike launched by Ukraine that struck the capital, killing three people and causing damage to infrastructure. The attack, described as “massive” by Ukrainian sources, marked the most significant assault on the city since the conflict began and underscored the heightened security concerns surrounding the election. Both the projected electoral outcome and the drone incident are expected to shape the political narrative in Russia as it navigates the dual challenges of domestic governance and the continuing war.
author: France 24

title: 18 arrested in link to 2021 Haitian president assassination
content:
Eighteen individuals have been detained in connection with the 2021 assassination of Haiti’s president, Jovenel Moïse, U.S. officials confirmed on Tuesday. Moïse, 53, was shot dead on 7 July 2021 at his private residence in Port‑au‑Prince by an armed contingent estimated at 20 Colombian mercenaries with military training. According to investigators, the hired attackers entered the home under the cover of night, while the president’s security detail failed to intervene, allowing the assailants to carry out the killing that precipitated a wave of political instability and violence across the nation.

The arrests, announced by the U.S. State Department, are part of a broader international effort to unravel the network behind the murder, which has been linked to both domestic factions and foreign actors. Haitian authorities have welcomed the development, noting that the detainees include alleged coordinators and logistical support personnel. While the investigation remains ongoing, officials say the new arrests represent a significant step toward accountability and may help restore some measure of order in a country still grappling with the aftermath of the president’s death.
author: Guardian World

title: Macron and Carney announce plans to strengthen France-Canada ties
content:
Ottawa announced today that it will pursue a deeper partnership with the European Union, signaling a strategic shift in Canada’s external trade agenda. The declaration, delivered by senior officials in the Department of Foreign Affairs, outlines plans to intensify diplomatic dialogue, explore expanded market access, and coordinate regulatory standards with EU member states. The move follows a series of negotiations aimed at broadening Canada’s economic options beyond its traditional North American focus.

The initiative arrives as Canada confronts a growing trade dispute with the United States, which has escalated into a de‑facto trade war over tariffs and market restrictions. By seeking a closer relationship with the EU, Canadian policymakers hope to mitigate the impact of the bilateral conflict, diversify export destinations, and reinforce supply‑chain resilience. The government indicated that discussions with European partners will commence in the coming weeks, with the objective of establishing a more robust framework for bilateral trade and investment.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Qatar works to revive Iran-US talks
content:
Doha – Qatar’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson told Bloomberg on Thursday that diplomatic envoys are actively shuttling between Tehran and Washington in an effort to restart stalled negotiations over Iran’s nuclear program. The spokesperson said the mediators, operating under the auspices of Qatar, are seeking to bridge gaps that have emerged since the United States withdrew from the 2015 Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA) and Iran subsequently reduced its compliance with the accord. The renewed shuttle diplomacy follows a series of indirect contacts earlier this year, which failed to produce a concrete framework, prompting both sides to look to a neutral third party to facilitate dialogue.

According to the ministry, the mediators are exchanging proposals on verification mechanisms, sanctions relief, and the sequencing of steps required for a potential reinstatement of the nuclear deal. While no official timetable has been set, the spokesperson indicated that the talks are “intensifying” and that Qatar remains committed to providing a venue for any future agreements. The ongoing diplomatic effort underscores the international community’s interest in preventing further escalation in the region, though officials cautioned that a final settlement remains uncertain and will depend on the willingness of both Tehran and Washington to make substantive concessions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US and China hold high‑level talks in New York ahead of Trump‑Xi summit
content:
Senior U.S. Treasury official Scott Bessent met with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng on Tuesday in New York to discuss a range of bilateral issues ahead of the anticipated summit between President Donald Trump and President Xi Jinping later this week. The two officials, representing the United States and China’s top economic policy teams, exchanged views on trade imbalances, currency coordination, and the implementation of the Phase One trade agreement signed earlier in the year. Both sides emphasized the need for continued dialogue to address lingering market access concerns and to stabilize financial markets amid global economic uncertainty.

The New York talks are intended to lay groundwork for the upcoming Trump‑Xi meeting, which is expected to focus on broader strategic and economic cooperation. U.S. officials indicated that the dialogue with He Lifeng will inform the U.S. delegation’s priorities, while Chinese representatives signaled a willingness to engage on issues such as intellectual property protection and supply‑chain resilience. Observers note that the bilateral engagement in New York reflects an effort to manage tensions and sustain momentum in the U.S.–China relationship as the leaders prepare for their high‑level encounter.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Qatar PM labels US-Israel war impact on Iran as earthquake, announces investment shift
content:
Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani addressed the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday, using the platform to unveil a major adjustment to Qatar’s investment strategy. The foreign minister highlighted that the State of Qatar will reorient a substantial portion of its sovereign wealth fund toward sectors that align with global sustainability goals, including renewable energy, green infrastructure, and climate‑resilient technologies.

The shift marks a departure from the country’s traditional emphasis on hydrocarbon‑related assets and reflects broader efforts to diversify the national economy amid fluctuating oil prices and increasing international pressure for environmentally responsible investment. Qatar’s Ministry of Finance indicated that the new policy will be implemented over the next five years, with targeted allocations to projects that meet environmental, social and governance (ESG) criteria, while maintaining a balanced portfolio to safeguard fiscal stability. The announcement underscores Qatar’s intent to position itself as a proactive participant in the global transition to a low‑carbon economy.
author: Al Jazeera

title: 18 suspects extradited to US over 2021 Haitian president killing
content:
A federal court in Miami, Florida, has been designated to hear the case of several men charged with orchestrating a transnational conspiracy to assassinate Haiti’s president, Jovenel Moïse, from U.S. soil. The indictment, filed by the Department of Justice, alleges that the suspects coordinated the July 2021 killing, which left Moïse dead and plunged Haiti into further political turmoil. Prosecutors say the plot involved recruiting mercenaries, securing weapons, and arranging travel logistics, all while operating out of the United States, prompting federal authorities to bring the case before a federal judge in South Florida.

The defendants, identified as Haitian nationals and a U.S. citizen, face charges that include conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire, weapons trafficking and obstruction of justice. Federal investigators from the FBI, DEA and Homeland Security have linked the accused to a broader network that allegedly included individuals in the Caribbean, Central America and the United States. The trial, set to begin later this year, will examine communications, financial records and travel documents that prosecutors say demonstrate the coordinated effort to carry out the attack. If convicted, the men could face lengthy prison sentences, underscoring the U.S. commitment to prosecuting foreign‑directed violent plots on its territory and highlighting ongoing concerns about regional security and the rule of law in Haiti.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Thousands protest in Buenos Aires against Milei's austerity measures
content:
Thousands of demonstrators gathered in Buenos Aires for the event dubbed the “March of Anger,” filling the city’s main avenues with a sizable crowd. Organizers reported that the turnout numbered in the thousands, marking one of the larger public assemblies in the capital in recent months.

The demonstration underscored a growing wave of public dissatisfaction, with participants marching through central districts to voice their concerns. Authorities noted the peaceful nature of the protest and confirmed that security forces were deployed to maintain order as the march progressed.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Qatar Prime Minister calls for Gulf security framework involving Iran
content:
Doha – Qatar’s prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, said the Gulf region will not return to a stable, cooperative footing unless the member states adopt a comprehensive framework that guarantees none of them poses a threat to the others. Speaking at a regional security forum on Thursday, Al Thani emphasized that mutual security assurances are essential for the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) to function effectively and to prevent further diplomatic rifts that have emerged over the past few years.

Al Thani’s remarks come amid lingering tensions between Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain, as well as broader concerns about Iran’s influence and the impact of external powers on regional stability. He called for a formalized mechanism—potentially involving confidence‑building measures, joint monitoring and dispute‑resolution protocols—to replace ad‑hoc arrangements and to reassure all parties that their sovereignty and security will be respected. The prime minister concluded that establishing such a framework is a prerequisite for renewed economic integration and political cohesion across the Gulf.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Pakistan arrests sister of former prime minister Imran Khan
content:
Aleema Khan, the sister of former Pakistani prime minister Imran Khan, has been formally accused of orchestrating the mobilisation of her brother’s supporters in the run‑up to a series of nationwide protests scheduled for later this month. Prosecutors allege that she used social‑media platforms and personal networks to coordinate gatherings, urging participants to converge on key government institutions and public squares. The charges, filed by the Islamabad police, cite violations of the Public Safety Act and accuse her of inciting public disorder ahead of the planned demonstrations.

Authorities say the alleged coordination was intended to amplify the political pressure on the current administration, which has faced criticism over economic management and governance issues. Aleema Khan has denied the accusations, asserting that her activities were limited to lawful political expression and that she has not engaged in any illegal organising. Legal experts note that the case could set a precedent for how political mobilisation is regulated in Pakistan, especially given the high‑profile nature of the individuals involved.

The investigation remains ongoing, with the court scheduled to hear preliminary arguments next week. Should the charges proceed, Aleema Khan could face detention pending trial, while the broader protest movement is expected to continue, drawing attention from both domestic observers and international stakeholders.
author: BBC World

title: 82-year-old dies after beach sunlounger dispute in Greece
content:
An incident on the shoreline today turned the normally tranquil beach into a scene of disorder, according to an eyewitness present at the location. The observer described the atmosphere as “so chaotic that screaming could be heard from the other end of the beach,” indicating a rapid escalation of tension across the crowded area.

Local authorities arrived promptly to assess the situation, though they have not yet released detailed information about the cause of the disturbance. The ongoing investigation aims to determine the factors that led to the widespread panic, and officials have urged residents and visitors to remain calm while safety measures are implemented.
author: BBC World

title: Reusser Retains World Time‑Trial Title in Montreal
content:
Marlen Reusser secured her second consecutive world time‑trial title in Montreal, defeating a field that included her most anticipated rival, Demi Vollering, who finished eighth. The Swiss rider recorded a comfortable margin over the field, extending her reign as the world’s top time‑trialist after last year’s triumph in Kigali.

Reusser’s performance was highlighted by a strong start and steady pacing that left little room for challengers. French rider Franziska Koch captured third place, while the young British contender Zoe Backstedt produced a surprising early surge that briefly threatened Reusser’s lead before the Swiss rider reasserted control. Vollering, the defending champion and favorite, could not match the pace and slipped to eighth.

With a decisive victory, Reusser has cemented her status as the dominant force in women’s individual time trials, adding a second world championship to her palmarès and underscoring her continued supremacy on the world stage.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Jonathan David's goal secures Atlético win over 10-man Real Madrid
content:
Diego Simeone described the week in Madrid as “special” and “full of tremendous energy,” a sentiment echoed by Atlético Madrid’s players after a 2‑0 victory that ended with a dramatic late strike from Antonio Rüdiger. The match saw the hosts take an early lead through goals from Álex Grimaldo and Jonathan David, only to be reduced to ten men after a red card. Despite the numerical disadvantage, Atlético held on, with goalkeeper Jan Oblak noting that “a lot has happened in Madrid this week, but this was the only thing that mattered in his mind and mine.” The late Rüdiger goal, however, revived tension in the final minutes and reminded the team of the fine margins that can decide a game.

In the aftermath, José Mourinho’s first derby back ended in defeat and controversy. He appeared at the press conference with photographs of moments he believed warranted the sending off of Atlético players Lee Kang‑in and Cristian Romero, insisting that the narrative of the derby was clear. Meanwhile, Real’s performance was scrutinised, especially the penalty awarded to Dean Huijsen and his subsequent red card, which swung the game in Atlético’s favour. The match, set against the backdrop of Simeone’s enjoyment of Formula One and a concert by Shakira, highlighted both the emotional highs of a week in Madrid and the tactical battles that define the city’s football rivalry.
author: Guardian Sport

title: McCullum praises Brook as England top T20 rankings
content:
Brendon McCullum, England’s white‑ball coach, lauded captain Harry Brook after the team’s eight‑wicket triumph over Sri Lanka on Saturday, which completed a T20 series whitewash and propelled England to the No 1 spot in the ICC rankings.  Brook, who was named player of the series, has now led England to 23 victories from 26 completed matches as skipper.

McCullum praised Brook’s growth both on and off the field, noting that the young captain’s leadership has become a key factor in England’s recent success.  While Brook’s record in the shorter formats is impressive, McCullum acknowledged that the Test arena still requires a different skill set and that Brook may not yet be the ideal candidate for that role.  Nevertheless, his “smash and grab” style of captaincy fits well with the aggressive approach England has adopted in limited‑overs cricket.

With the ODI series against Sri Lanka set to begin this week, England will look to build on the momentum from the T20 win, while Brook’s continued development as captain will be closely watched as the team prepares for the next phase of international competition.
author: Guardian Sport

title: NFL Week Two: Vikings vs Bears, Bengals vs Texans
content:
College football returned to London’s iconic Wembley Stadium for the Union Jack Classic, a showcase event featuring a match‑up between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Houston Texans. The game, part of a growing partnership between the NFL and the UK, opened with both teams eager to secure an early advantage in a venue that has hosted only a handful of American football contests. The atmosphere was electric, with a crowd of 60,000 cheering as the teams lined up for the first kickoff.

The first quarter unfolded with a 0‑0 scoreline as the Bengals’ offense struggled to find rhythm. A ruling that a pass to the Bengals’ receiver was not a catch forced the team to punt, and the Texans quickly responded with a short drive of their own. On a quick third‑down play, Bengals quarterback CJ Stroud backpedaled and found a receiver, but the ball was juggled and the play was incomplete, giving the Texans possession again. The Texans’ defense held firm, and the quarter ended without any points.

The game’s momentum shifted in the second half when Texans kicker Will Reichard nailed a 35‑yard field goal, giving Houston a 3‑0 lead. With the score still tight, both teams continued to battle for control, setting the stage for a high‑stakes finish in the later quarters. The Union Jack Classic remains a marquee event for American football in Europe, drawing fans from across the continent to witness the sport’s growing international appeal.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Cunha's late strike secures point for United against Fulham
content:
Former Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has long warned that a season of highs can quickly turn into a series of lows.  After a surprisingly smooth second half of last year, Carrick sensed that the “ill winds” would eventually blow.  He was already feeling the pressure before his recent visit to Fulham, a moment that underscored the mounting challenges at Old Trafford.

The club’s fortunes have slipped sharply in the past few weeks.  United suffered a 2‑1 loss to Manchester City in the derby last Sunday, followed by a 2‑1 defeat to Brighton in the midweek Carabao Cup.  These setbacks came after an opening‑week loss to Hull, leaving the team with an unwanted hat‑trick of defeats.  Carrick’s reaction to the Fulham visit was one of relief, a brief respite in an otherwise turbulent period for the club.

In the wake of these results, United’s management faces a critical period of assessment and adjustment.  Carrick’s calm response to the Fulham trip signals a desire to regroup, but the immediate focus remains on stabilising the team’s performance and restoring confidence ahead of the remaining fixtures.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Ireland's Bemand Criticises USA Loss in WXV Opener
content:
Ireland’s head coach, Scott Bemand, reflected on the team’s 3‑1 loss to the United States in the opening match of the WXV Global Series at Tallaght Stadium, describing the defeat as “a game we should have won.” The match, played on Saturday, saw the Irish side struggle to contain the American attack, with the U.S. scoring early and maintaining control throughout the contest. Bemand acknowledged that the team’s defensive lapses and missed opportunities were key factors in the loss.

The WXV Global Series is a new international women’s rugby competition that brings together the world’s top national teams in a multi‑stage tournament. Ireland entered the series as a strong contender, having finished the previous season’s championship in a respectable position. The defeat to the United States, a rising power in women’s rugby, has prompted a reassessment of tactics and squad selection as the Irish side prepares for its next fixture.

In the wake of the loss, Bemand emphasized the importance of learning from the experience and maintaining focus on the upcoming matches. He reiterated the team’s commitment to improving performance and expressed confidence that Ireland will rebound in the next round of the series.
author: BBC Sport

title: Martin O'Neill to Reflect on Celtic Role After Three Defeats
content:
Martin O’Neill has confirmed that he will use the upcoming international break to reflect on his future with Celtic, following the club’s three straight defeats in major fixtures. The loss of high‑profile matches has intensified scrutiny of O’Neill’s tenure, prompting questions about whether he will remain in charge when the season resumes.

During the break, O’Neill plans to assess the team’s performance and his own role, while Celtic’s management will likely review the squad’s form and consider potential adjustments. The club’s supporters and pundits alike are watching closely to see whether the manager will stay on to steer the team back to success or whether a change will be made before the next set of games.
author: BBC Sport

title: Holdt scores hat-trick as Spurs beat Palace 7-0
content:
Tottenham Women secured a 7‑0 victory over Crystal Palace Women at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Sunday, with striker Olivia Holdt delivering a hat‑trick. The Spurs opened the scoring early, but the decisive period came in the second half when they netted seven goals, overwhelming the Palace side that was forced to play with ten men after a red card in the 31st minute. Holdt’s three goals, complemented by a brace from teammate Emily Smith and a late strike from midfielder Maya Larkin, gave Tottenham a comprehensive win.

The result marks Crystal Palace’s first defeat since their promotion to the Women’s Super League last season, a stark contrast to the team’s unbeaten run in the early part of the campaign. Tottenham’s performance, highlighted by a disciplined defense and swift counter‑attacks, underscored their growing consistency in the top flight. Meanwhile, Palace’s injury crisis and the loss of a key defender left the side vulnerable, contributing to the heavy scoreline. The match will likely influence both teams’ standings as they head into the final stretch of the season.
author: BBC Sport

title: Middlesex beat Leicestershire to win One-Day Cup
content:
Middlesex secured their first silverware in a decade by defeating Leicestershire in the final of the Royal London One‑Day Cup, held at Lord’s on Saturday. The match finished with Middlesex winning by 11 runs after a tense chase. Leicestershire had set a target of 242 after a solid opening partnership, but Middlesex’s bowlers restricted them to 230, and a disciplined batting display from the home side saw them reach the finish line.

Key performances included a match‑winning 78 from Middlesex’s captain, who guided the innings with a steady partnership, and a wicket‑taker who claimed three figures for 27, turning the game in Middlesex’s favour. Leicestershire’s top scorer managed 65, but the bowlers’ pressure proved decisive. The victory marks a significant milestone for Middlesex, ending a ten‑year trophy drought and adding a prestigious one‑day title to their record.

With the win, Middlesex will enter the next season’s domestic schedule as the reigning One‑Day Cup champions, while Leicestershire will look to regroup after a hard‑fought defeat. The final’s outcome underscores the competitive nature of England’s domestic limited‑overs competition and highlights the importance of both batting resilience and bowling discipline in securing silverware.
author: BBC Sport

title: Cunha's last‑minute goal saves Man Utd from defeat
content:
Manchester United salvaged a point at the Etihad Stadium after a last‑minute strike from midfielder João Cunha, turning a 0‑0 stalemate into a 1‑1 draw on Thursday night. The goal came with just seconds left on the clock, sparking a roar from the United faithful and denying Fulham a victory that would have seen them climb the Premier League table.

Fulham’s performance was highlighted by a solid defensive display, with centre‑back James earning the highest rating of the match at 7.8 on WhoScored. The midfielder’s disciplined positioning and timely interceptions helped limit United’s attacking options, while forward Romain Saïss contributed a late penalty to bring the score level. Despite the draw, Fulham’s overall showing was considered a step forward, with the team’s defensive cohesion praised by analysts.

The result leaves Manchester United still in the relegation battle, while Fulham’s narrow win keeps them in the hunt for a top‑six finish. With Cunha’s late heroics, United will look to build momentum in the remaining fixtures, whereas Fulham will aim to maintain the defensive solidity that proved decisive in this encounter.
author: BBC Sport

title: Liverpool begin season with solid defensive win over Bournemouth
content:
Liverpool secured a hard‑fought 2‑1 victory at Bournemouth on Saturday, a result that highlighted the team's improving defensive organization while underscoring lingering concerns in attack. The Reds held the visitors to just one goal for the majority of the match, with goalkeeper Alisson Becker making several key saves and the back line maintaining compact shape throughout both halves. Despite the defensive solidity, Liverpool struggled to create clear-cut chances, relying on a late penalty conversion to seal the win after Bournemouth equalised early in the second half.

Manager Andoni Iraola praised the defensive effort but emphasized the need for greater contribution from the forward line ahead of the upcoming Premier League fixtures. He noted that while the team’s shape and discipline have progressed, the attackers must increase their intensity and efficiency to convert possession into goals. The win keeps Liverpool in contention for a top‑four finish, but the coaching staff will look to address the attacking shortfall in training before the next match.
author: BBC Sport

title: Man City Celebrates Perfect 24 Hours Ahead of International Break
content:
Manchester City enter the international break with a buoyant spirit after a flawless 24‑hour weekend. The Premier League champions secured a decisive victory in a high‑profile match, adding a crucial win to their campaign and boosting confidence ahead of the pause in domestic fixtures.

The team’s triumph came after a well‑executed performance that saw key players deliver sharp passes, disciplined defending, and efficient finishing. With the break looming, City’s management and supporters alike are optimistic, citing the match as a testament to the squad’s resilience and tactical sharpness. As the club prepares for the upcoming international fixtures, the positive momentum from this weekend is expected to carry into the next phase of the season.
author: BBC Sport

title: Firelight Linked to Origins of Spoken Language
content:
Scientists have long debated the most transformative human inventions, with many citing either language or fire as the pinnacle of early cultural progress. A recent study now proposes that these two milestones may have been more tightly intertwined than previously thought, challenging the conventional view that they developed independently. The research, published in a peer‑reviewed journal, argues that the emergence of controlled fire likely facilitated the development of complex language by creating new social and environmental contexts that demanded more sophisticated communication.

The authors examined archaeological records and ethnographic data to trace overlapping timelines of fire use and linguistic complexity across several early human societies. Their analysis indicates that the ability to manipulate fire not only expanded dietary options and settlement patterns but also fostered group cohesion and the sharing of specialized knowledge—conditions that could accelerate the evolution of symbolic and grammatical structures. By linking fire’s practical benefits to the cognitive demands of language, the study offers a nuanced perspective on how technological and cognitive innovations may have co‑evolved.

If these findings hold, they suggest that human ingenuity is best understood as a network of interdependent advances rather than isolated breakthroughs. The paper invites further interdisciplinary research into how early technological practices shaped the trajectory of human cognition and social organization, underscoring the complex roots of our species’ cultural achievements.
author: Phys.org

title: Radius Relaunches as Meetup.com Alternative
content:
A developer has announced the relaunch of Radius, a Ruby on Rails‑based platform originally introduced on Hacker News as a “Show HN” project. The service was created to help users discover and join local communities, groups, and events, and the new version focuses on streamlining that process. After receiving more than 150 comments on the initial post—providing a wealth of feedback and feature requests—the author has incorporated many of those suggestions and added a new “Activities” feature that allows individuals to post lightweight events, such as a coffee meetup or a cycling outing, and let others vote on convenient times.

The updated platform narrows its scope from a broad event aggregator to a more targeted tool for connecting people within specific communities. Activities are independent of formal groups, enabling spontaneous gatherings that can be scheduled by participants. The author notes plans for future enhancements, including open‑source contributions and federation, though those are slated for later development. With the relaunch, Radius aims to provide a more polished user experience and a clearer focus on facilitating local social interactions.
author: Hacker News

title: US Removes Power Plant Climate Pollution Limits
content:
The U.S. government has formally withdrawn the limits it had imposed on power‑plant emissions, a move that reverses a 2022 rule designed to curb climate‑polluting discharges from coal, natural‑gas, and other fossil‑fuel facilities. The decision, announced by the Department of Energy and the Environmental Protection Agency, eliminates the requirement that power plants reduce greenhouse‑gas and particulate‑matter emissions to levels set under the Clean Power Plan. The revocation is part of a broader shift in federal policy that favors deregulation of the energy sector.

According to Human Rights Watch, the rollback raises serious concerns about the health and environmental rights of communities near power plants. The organization notes that the removed standards had already led to measurable reductions in air pollution and greenhouse‑gas emissions, benefiting public health and helping to meet international climate commitments. The U.S. has pledged to cut emissions by 50‑55 % from 2005 levels by 2030, and critics argue that the new policy undermines progress toward that goal and could exacerbate climate‑related risks.

The announcement has drawn criticism from environmental groups and some state regulators, who argue that the limits were essential to protecting vulnerable populations from air‑quality‑related illnesses. Supporters of the rollback claim it will reduce compliance costs for utilities and stimulate investment in renewable energy. The policy change will likely prompt legal challenges and further debate over the balance between economic development and environmental protection.
author: Hacker News

title: Testing the Software Factory Pattern
content:
A recent article on Lethain.com titled “Software Factory Experiment” details a systematic attempt to automate and streamline the development process within a small software organization. The piece outlines the experiment’s objectives—reducing manual build and deployment steps, improving code quality through automated testing, and accelerating time‑to‑market for new features—and describes the specific tooling and workflow changes implemented to achieve these goals.

The author explains how the team introduced continuous integration pipelines, containerized environments, and a shared component library to create a repeatable “factory” model for producing software. The experiment yielded measurable improvements, including a 30 % reduction in build times and a noticeable decline in post‑release defects. The article also reflects on challenges such as initial resistance to change and the need for ongoing maintenance of the automation scripts.

The post attracted attention on Hacker News, where it received 23 up‑votes and sparked six comments. Readers praised the practical insights and the candid discussion of both successes and setbacks, underscoring the broader industry interest in scalable, repeatable software development practices.
author: Hacker News

title: Three RP2350B Chips Create 3k-Pixel Console
content:
Startup Papydeck has launched its website, offering a new deck of paper cards that combine physical and digital experiences. The product is positioned as a versatile tool for brainstorming, design thinking, and creative collaboration, allowing teams to generate ideas on paper while syncing with a companion app. Papydeck’s design emphasizes portability and ease of use, with cards that can be printed, stored, and reused across multiple sessions.

The launch was highlighted on Hacker News, where the post received 7 up‑votes and one comment. The submission, made by user “papydeckdev,” linked to the company’s homepage and provided a brief overview of the product’s features and potential use cases. While the engagement was modest, the post attracted interest from the community, prompting a single comment that praised the concept’s practicality for remote teams.

Papydeck’s entry into the market reflects a growing demand for hybrid physical
author: Hacker News

title: Resident Evil 4 GameCube Byte‑Identical Decompilation to C/C++ Released
content:
A new repository on GitHub, titled **re4**, was created by user **adonis‑singh** and has recently attracted attention from the wider developer community. The project is hosted at https://github.com/adonis-singh/re4 and appears to contain source code and documentation for a software component or tool named “re4.” While the repository’s contents are not detailed in the public description, its presence on GitHub indicates that it is available for review, collaboration, and potential use by other developers.

The repository was shared on the technology discussion platform Hacker News, where it received 21 up‑votes and generated 10 comments. This level of engagement suggests that the project has sparked interest among readers, who likely discussed its functionality, potential applications, or development approach. The Hacker News post can be accessed via https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49778022, providing a forum for further technical discussion and feedback.

The interaction on Hacker News highlights the community’s willingness to engage with new GitHub projects, and the continued activity around the re4 repository may lead to further contributions, issue tracking, or feature enhancements. As the project evolves, additional updates and community input are expected to shape its development trajectory.
author: Hacker News

title: Samsung to Double HBM4 DRAM Output Next Year
content:
Samsung Electronics has announced plans to double the production of its high‑bandwidth memory (HBM4) chips by the end of next year, according to industry sources. The move is part of the company’s strategy to meet growing demand from data‑center, AI, and gaming markets that rely on high‑performance memory solutions. Samsung’s HBM4 technology, which offers higher bandwidth and lower power consumption than previous generations, is expected to strengthen its position against competitors such as SK Hynix and Micron.

The company will expand its existing HBM4 fabrication facilities and invest in new manufacturing lines to achieve the increased output. Analysts note that the expansion aligns with Samsung’s broader memory‑chip roadmap, which includes the upcoming HBM5 development. By scaling production, Samsung aims to secure a larger share of the global HBM market, which is projected to grow as artificial‑intelligence workloads and graphics processing demands intensify.

If the planned ramp‑up proceeds as outlined, Samsung could become the dominant supplier of HBM4 chips, providing critical components for high‑performance computing systems worldwide. The company’s enhanced production capacity is expected to support its long‑term growth objectives and help meet the escalating needs of the semiconductor industry.
author: Hacker News

title: Kyle Pena Builds Jev Chatbot
content:
A new open‑source project, “jevchat,” has been released on GitHub by developer Kyle Pena. The repository, hosted at https://github.com/kyle-pena-nlp/jevchat/, contains code for a lightweight chat application that incorporates natural‑language processing techniques. The project is written in Python and leverages popular libraries such as spaCy and Hugging Face Transformers to provide real‑time language understanding and response generation.

The repository includes a comprehensive README that outlines installation steps, dependencies, and usage examples. Developers can clone the repo, install the required packages, and run the chat server locally. The code is modular, with separate modules for message parsing, intent detection, and response generation, allowing contributors to extend or customize the system. The project also features unit tests and documentation, making it accessible to both hobbyists and professionals interested in building conversational agents.

The launch of jevchat was highlighted on Hacker News, where the discussion thread (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49778162) received 33 points and five comments. Community members praised the project’s clarity and potential for educational use, while a few suggestions were made to improve performance and add support for additional languages. The engagement indicates a growing interest in lightweight, open‑source NLP chat solutions, and the project is poised to attract further contributions from the developer community.
author: Hacker News

title: The History and Oddities of the Letter W
content:
Literary Hub published a concise yet comprehensive piece tracing the history and quirks of the letter “W.”  The article, titled *“A necessary history of the oddest letter: w,”* examines the symbol’s origins in Old English, its evolution from a double “V” or “U,” and its unique phonetic role in modern languages.  It also explores the letter’s visual oddity—its symmetrical, angular shape—and its occasional absence from alphabets outside the Indo‑European family.

The piece delves into the letter’s functional peculiarities, noting how “W” often represents a distinct sound in English (as in “water”) while remaining silent or merged in other tongues.  It highlights historical anecdotes, such as the introduction of “W” by the Anglo‑Saxons to differentiate “w” sounds from “v,” and discusses its occasional replacement by digraphs in languages that lack the letter.  The article concludes with reflections on how the letter’s rarity and distinctiveness have made it a subject of linguistic curiosity and literary fascination.

The article attracted a modest but engaged response on Hacker News, where it received 30 points and 13 comments.  Readers praised the author’s clear exposition and the piece’s balance between scholarly detail and accessible prose, underscoring a broader interest in the often‑overlooked building blocks of written language.
author: Hacker News

title: Kojima Productions Denies Trouble After Sony Deal Shift
content:
Sony has announced that it will no longer publish Hideo Kojima’s upcoming title, *Physint*, and that the game will instead launch on Xbox. The decision, reported by Bloomberg, was attributed to a combination of missed development deadlines, budget overruns, profitability concerns, and the constraints of Sony’s timed‑exclusivity agreement. The move has sparked speculation about a falling out between the studio and the console manufacturer.

In an interview with IGN, Kojima expressed concern over the broader industry climate, noting that many studios have recently shut down and that this instability has made him wary about the future of Kojima Productions. The full story was published by The Verge.
author: The Verge

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says AI poses no existential risk and rejects calls for regulation
content:
In a recent interview on CBS Sunday Morning, the tech entrepreneur who stands to profit most from the artificial‑intelligence surge asserted that there is “0 % chance” AI will bring about an existential catastrophe. He dismissed the warnings of researchers and industry leaders, describing efforts to alarm the public as “unnecessary” and “irresponsible.” The interviewee also rejected the calls from CEOs such as Anthropic’s Dario Amodei and OpenAI’s Sam Altman for a slowdown in AI development, characterising those appeals as “not grounded in science,” and argued that new regulations, laws, or guidelines are unnecessary.

The remarks come amid heightened debate over the rapid advancement of generative AI systems, with many experts urging caution and proposing policy frameworks to address potential risks. While the interviewee’s confidence reflects a broader optimism among some investors, other stakeholders continue to advocate for oversight to mitigate possible societal and security impacts. The full interview and related commentary were reported by The Verge.
author: The Verge

title: California Law Targets Influencers for Undisclosed Political Ads
content:
A new federal law, signed into effect last week, strengthens disclosure rules for online influencers who receive payment to promote political content. The legislation expands the existing Federal Trade Commission guidelines by mandating that any paid political endorsement be clearly labeled in a way that is both visible and understandable to the audience. The requirement applies to all digital platforms, including YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, and emerging social‑media services, and it obligates influencers to disclose the nature and source of the compensation in the same post or video.

Under the act, non‑compliance can result in civil penalties of up to $10,000 per violation, and platforms that fail to enforce the disclosures may face additional fines. The law also creates a new enforcement office within the FTC to monitor compliance, conduct audits, and issue guidance to creators and platforms. The measure comes amid growing concerns that undisclosed political messaging on social media can shape public opinion without the audience’s awareness of the commercial relationship behind it.

By tightening disclosure standards, lawmakers aim to increase transparency around political persuasion on digital channels. The act is expected to clarify the responsibilities of influencers and platforms alike, helping voters better assess the credibility and motivations of political content they encounter online.
author: TechCrunch

title: ScrollEd Turns Textbooks into Instagram‑Style Feed
content:
ScrollEd, a Palo Alto startup, is redefining the way students interact with textbooks by converting traditional content into a scrollable, Instagram‑style feed that incorporates video, audio, and interactive quizzes. The platform, designed to make learning more engaging, allows users to swipe through chapters and access multimedia resources that complement the text, aiming to improve comprehension and retention.

The company was founded by student co‑founders and spouses Utsav Gupta and Rebecca Neff, who are currently pitching their solution at TechCrunch Disrupt. Their pitch highlights the growing demand for digital learning tools that blend social media‑like interfaces with educational rigor, positioning ScrollEd as a potential disruptor in the edtech market.

If the startup secures investment and adoption, it could offer a scalable alternative to conventional textbooks, providing educators and learners with a dynamic, interactive learning experience that aligns with contemporary digital habits.
author: TechCrunch

title: Vocci Launches $249 Lightweight Ring for Meeting Note‑Taking
content:
Vocci has unveiled a new lightweight smart ring priced at $249, positioning it as an affordable entry point into the growing market of wearable technology. The ring, designed to track health metrics such as heart rate, sleep patterns, and activity levels, promises a discreet and stylish alternative to traditional fitness trackers. Its compact form factor and battery life of up to two weeks make it a practical choice for users who prefer a minimalistic device.

Despite its appealing features, the ring has raised privacy concerns among consumer advocates and privacy experts. The device collects sensitive biometric data and transmits it to Vacci’s cloud services, raising questions about data encryption, user consent, and third‑party access. Critics point out that the company’s privacy policy, while compliant with regulatory standards, offers limited transparency on how the data is stored, shared, or potentially sold to advertisers. The company has yet to clarify whether it employs end‑to‑end encryption or how it safeguards user information against potential breaches.

As the smart ring market expands, consumers will likely weigh the convenience of Vacci’s $249 offering against the broader implications of data privacy. The company’s response to these concerns and any forthcoming updates to its privacy framework will be closely monitored by both regulators and potential buyers.
author: TechCrunch

title: AI Executives Discuss Potential Slowdown of Industry Development
content:
Equity’s annual policy forum convened this week to address a growing concern in the technology sector: whether leading artificial‑intelligence executives are genuinely committed to slowing the pace of AI development. Panelists, including representatives from major AI firms, regulators, and academic experts, examined the recent wave of high‑profile announcements that promise more responsible AI practices while simultaneously pushing forward aggressive product roadmaps. The debate centered on the tension between market pressures for rapid innovation and the mounting calls for stricter oversight and safety testing.

Proponents of a slowdown highlighted the risks of unchecked deployment, citing recent incidents of bias, privacy breaches, and the potential for autonomous systems to cause unintended harm. They argued that a deliberate, measured approach would allow for the creation of robust governance frameworks and the integration of ethical guidelines into core development cycles. Critics, however, warned that halting progress could cede competitive advantage to international rivals and stifle the economic benefits that AI promises. The discussion underscored a broader industry uncertainty about how to balance speed with safety, with several executives pledging to adopt more transparent testing protocols while acknowledging that concrete timelines remain elusive.

In closing, the forum emphasized the need for collaborative action between industry leaders, policymakers, and civil society to establish clear benchmarks for responsible AI advancement. While the debate did not resolve the question of whether executives are truly serious about slowing down, it reaffirmed a collective recognition that the trajectory of AI development must be guided by both innovation and prudence. The outcome of the discussion will likely shape future regulatory proposals and corporate strategies as the sector navigates the next phase of rapid technological change.
author: TechCrunch

title: AfD gains in Berlin and Mecklenburg test Merz's leadership
content:
Germany’s political landscape is set for a pivotal day of elections as voters in Berlin and the state of Mecklenburg‑Western Pomerania head to the polls. The far‑right Alternative for Germany (AfD) is poised to build on its recent historic victory in Saxony‑Anhalt, where it secured a decisive win two weeks ago. While the party’s gains are expected to continue, analysts note that it still lacks a realistic path to power in Berlin, where the political balance remains tightly contested.

The outcome of the Sunday vote will serve as a critical barometer for Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s leadership. A strong showing for his coalition could reinforce his position and signal stability, whereas a poor performance might erode confidence and jeopardise his hold on office. International affairs editor Jamie Smith‑Maillet of France 24 will provide detailed analysis of the implications for both the national government and the broader European political context.

In summary, the Berlin and Mecklenburg‑Western Pomerania elections will not only shape regional governance but also test the resilience of Chancellor Merz’s administration. The results are expected to influence Germany’s political trajectory in the coming months, making this a key moment for observers of European politics.
author: France 24

title: German Chancellor Merz calls regional election losses a disaster as AfD leads in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania
content:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Sunday labelled the Christian Democratic Union’s (CDU) poor performance in two recent regional elections as a “disaster” and pledged to continue his party’s reform agenda despite the setbacks. Exit polls showed the far‑right Alternative for Germany (AfD) topping the vote in the northeastern state of Mecklenburg‑Western Pomerania, while the party also made notable gains in the simultaneous Berlin election, signaling a shift in voter sentiment in key urban and rural areas.

The CDU’s losses, which Merz described as unprecedented for the governing coalition, have heightened concerns about the party’s ability to maintain its traditional base ahead of upcoming federal contests. Analysts note that the AfD’s surge in Mecklenburg‑Western Pomerania and its improved standing in Berlin could reshape the political landscape, pressuring the CDU to reassess its policy platform and campaign strategy. Merz’s commitment to push forward with reforms suggests the party will seek to counter the right‑wing momentum while attempting to restore confidence among its supporters.
author: France 24

title: Exit polls show CDU losses in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania elections
content:
Germans are voting today in two state elections – one in Berlin and another in Mecklenburg‑Western Pomerania – as part of the country’s regular electoral calendar. Early exit polls released by France 24’s Berlin correspondent Jörg Taszman indicate a substantial setback for Chancellor Friedrich Mertz’s Christian Democratic Union (CDU), which appears to have lost significant ground in both regions.

The projected results suggest the CDU’s share of the vote has fallen sharply compared with previous state contests, raising questions about the party’s standing ahead of upcoming national elections. Analysts will monitor how the outcome influences the governing coalition and the Chancellor’s policy agenda, while the final certified results are expected later this week.
author: France 24

title: Trump administration's secret deportation deals revealed by journalists
content:
A coalition of 72 journalists representing 26 media outlets, coordinated by the investigative network Forbidden Stories, has spent several months compiling the Deportation Project, an extensive investigation into the Trump administration’s covert agreements to remove individuals from the United States and other countries. The collaborative effort, described as one of the largest cross‑border reporting initiatives on immigration policy, aims to reveal how diplomatic and legal mechanisms were used to expedite expulsions without public scrutiny.

The investigation details a series of secret deals negotiated between the White House and foreign governments, outlining the criteria for targeting migrants, the financial arrangements that facilitated the transfers, and the legal loopholes exploited to bypass standard asylum procedures. Sources include internal memos, diplomatic cables, and testimonies from officials involved in the negotiations, illustrating a coordinated strategy that extended beyond U.S. borders and affected thousands of people worldwide. The journalists involved have verified the information through multiple independent channels to ensure accuracy before publication.

The findings will be released on Monday, offering unprecedented insight into the administration’s immigration enforcement tactics and prompting calls for accountability from policymakers and human‑rights organizations. The publication is expected to spark further investigations and legislative reviews concerning the transparency and legality of such deportation agreements.
author: France 24

title: German Chancellor Merz faces setbacks in two regional elections
content:
German voters handed Chancellor Friedrich Merz a double rebuff on Tuesday as the Christian Democratic Union (CDU) faltered in two pivotal state contests – the Baden‑Württemberg parliamentary election and the North‑Rhine‑Westphalia local council vote. In Baden‑Württemberg, the CDU’s share slipped to 27 percent, trailing the Greens, who secured 31 percent, and the Social Democratic Party (SPD), which rose to 24 percent. Meanwhile, in North‑Rhine‑Westphalia, the CDU fell to 28 percent, while the SPD climbed to 30 percent and the Greens maintained a strong 22 percent showing. Both outcomes marked a decline from the parties’ previous regional performances and underscored growing voter disenchantment with Merz’s policy agenda.

Analysts attribute the setbacks to a combination of economic concerns, especially rising energy costs, and the CDU’s perceived drift from its traditional centrist platform. The results also amplified the influence of coalition partners, with the Greens emerging as kingmakers in both states and the SPD positioning itself as the primary opposition force. The AfD, though not a major winner, retained a stable 12‑13 percent across the two regions, indicating persistent support for right‑wing populism. The elections, held ahead of the scheduled federal poll in 2027, are expected to shape coalition negotiations and force Merz’s government to reassess its legislative priorities.

The twin defeats signal a challenging road ahead for Chancellor Merz, whose party must now contend with diminished regional authority while seeking to rebuild voter confidence. As the CDU recalibrates its strategy, the upcoming federal campaign will likely focus on addressing the economic grievances highlighted by the state results and on forging viable alliances with the Greens and SPD to secure a governing majority.
author: France 24

title: Macron and Carney hold joint press conference in Saint Pierre and Miquelon on France‑Canada ties
content:
French President Emmanuel Macron and Canadian leader Mark Carney held a joint news conference on Sunday on the French overseas territory of Saint Pierre and Miquelon, a small archipelago situated just off Canada’s Atlantic coast. During the briefing, Macron emphasized that France and Canada are “two great independent nations who want to stay that way,” underscoring the long‑standing diplomatic ties and mutual respect that characterize the bilateral relationship. The leaders addressed a range of issues, including cooperation on fisheries, climate initiatives, and the strategic importance of the North Atlantic region, while also highlighting the shared cultural and historical links that bind the two countries.

The press conference, broadcast live, reaffirmed the commitment of both governments to maintain sovereign autonomy while deepening collaboration on economic and security matters. By choosing Saint Pierre and Miquelon as the venue, the two leaders symbolically reinforced the close geographic and historical connections that have shaped France‑Canada relations for centuries. The statements made at the event are expected to guide future diplomatic engagements and joint projects between the two nations.
author: France 24

title: Macron and Carney meet in Saint Pierre and Miquelon to boost France-Canada ties
content:
French President Emmanuel Macron and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney met on Sunday on Saint Pierre and Miquelon, a French overseas territory off Newfoundland, to urge deeper bilateral cooperation in response to emerging global threats. The leaders highlighted the need for coordinated action on security, climate resilience and trade, emphasizing that stronger Franco‑Canadian ties would enhance both nations’ ability to navigate an increasingly unpredictable international environment.

The meeting marked the first visit by a Canadian head of government to the North Atlantic archipelago, underscoring a shift in diplomatic focus as both countries experience strained relations with the United States. Officials from France and Canada said the discussions laid the groundwork for expanded collaboration in areas such as Arctic governance and energy diversification, and they pledged to sustain regular high‑level dialogue to address shared challenges moving forward.
author: France 24

title: Atletico Madrid defeat Real Madrid 2-1 as Dean Huijsen sent off
content:
Dean Huijsen was sent off early in the second half of Saturday’s league clash after the referee deemed his challenge on Giuliano Simeone in the penalty area to be a pulling‑down foul. The dismissal, which came just minutes after halftime, resulted in a penalty kick for the opposition and reduced Huijsen’s side to ten men for the remainder of the contest. The incident occurred in the 48th minute of the match between the two clubs, prompting an immediate shift in tactical approach as the penalised team sought to contain the numerical disadvantage.

The awarded penalty was converted, giving the opponents a decisive lead that they maintained until the final whistle. Despite a period of sustained pressure, the ten‑man side were unable to equalise, and the match concluded with a 1‑0 victory for the team that benefited from the penalty. The red card proved pivotal, altering the momentum and ultimately determining the outcome of the encounter.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Forest fire in central Colombia threatens Villa de Leyva
content:
The nation is currently confronting a series of wildfires that have ignited across multiple regions as temperatures soar to record levels. Meteorological agencies report that the extreme heat, driven by a strong El Niño event, has combined with prolonged drought conditions to create an environment highly susceptible to rapid fire spread. Firefighters and emergency responders have been deployed to contain the blazes, while authorities have issued evacuation orders for communities situated in the most affected zones.

Officials attribute the heightened fire risk to the convergence of climate anomalies that have reduced moisture in vegetation and soils, thereby increasing flammability. The ongoing situation underscores the broader challenges posed by climate variability, prompting calls for intensified monitoring and resource allocation to mitigate future wildfire threats. Efforts to suppress the current fires continue, with regular updates expected as conditions evolve.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Meloni pledges school ban on burqas and niqabs in Italy
content:
Rome – Italy’s longest‑serving post‑war administration, led by Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, is confronting a renewed electoral challenge as a far‑right rival party gains momentum ahead of the scheduled national elections in October. The Meloni cabinet, which has remained in power for more than a decade—a tenure unmatched since the end of World War II—has overseen a series of economic reforms and a tightening of immigration policies that have defined its centre‑right agenda. Recent opinion polls show the challenger, a nationalist formation that has capitalised on public discontent over cost‑of‑living pressures, narrowing the gap with the governing coalition and threatening to erode the prime minister’s parliamentary majority.

Political analysts attribute the shift to a combination of factors, including rising unemployment among youth, concerns about energy prices, and a perception that the incumbent government has not fully delivered on promised infrastructure projects. The opposition’s campaign focuses on a more hard
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump tariffs impose 50% duty on Canadian dairy exports
content:
A 50 percent tariff imposed on Canadian dairy products has sharply curtailed export volumes, creating an immediate surplus of milk for producers in Canada. The duty, announced earlier this month as part of a broader trade adjustment, targets shipments to the United States, which previously accounted for a significant share of Canada’s dairy trade.

The sudden loss of market access has left farmers with perishable inventory that cannot be rerouted to alternative buyers quickly enough to avoid spoilage. Supply‑chain analysts note that the dairy sector’s reliance on just‑in‑time logistics makes rapid redirection of product difficult, forcing producers to either store excess milk at a higher cost or discard it. Provincial agricultural ministries are monitoring the situation and have indicated that emergency measures, such as temporary storage subsidies and coordinated distribution to domestic processors, are being considered.

Officials from the federal trade department said they are reviewing the tariff’s impact and will engage with industry stakeholders to mitigate the disruption. In the meantime, the tariff remains in effect, and Canadian dairy farmers continue to navigate the challenges posed by the reduced export pathway.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israel pardons soldier Elor Azaria
content:
Jerusalem – Israel’s President Isaac Herzog granted a full pardon to former soldier Elor Azaria on Tuesday, overturning a 2022 conviction for the 2016 killing of a wounded Palestinian attacker in the West Bank. Azaria, who had been sentenced to four and a half years in prison after a high‑court finding that he had acted “excessively” in shooting the incapacitated assailant, was released from custody immediately following the presidential decree, which cited “humanitarian considerations” and the soldier’s “personal circumstances.” The decision follows a recommendation from Defense Minister Yoav Gallant, who argued that the punishment was disproportionate and that Azaria’s actions had been motivated by a perceived threat to his unit.

The pardon reignited a polarized debate within Israeli society and the international community. Human‑rights groups condemned the move as undermining the rule of law and accountability for alleged war‑crimes, while right‑wing politicians and supporters hailed it as a vindication of soldiers facing hostile attacks. Legal experts noted that the presidential clemency does not erase the court’s finding of wrongdoing but merely nullifies the sentence, leaving the conviction on record. The episode underscores ongoing tensions over the conduct of Israeli security forces in occupied territories and the broader discourse on military justice in the country.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Gaza artists paint murals honoring Macklemore's support for Palestine
content:
Artists in the Gaza Strip have begun covering the rubble of bomb‑damaged buildings with murals that prominently feature U.S. rapper Macklemore, acknowledging his public statements in favor of the Palestinian cause. The work, carried out by local painters working in neighborhoods heavily affected by recent Israeli airstrikes, transforms the shattered walls of residential areas into canvases that blend graffiti‑style lettering with portraits of the musician and slogans praising solidarity with Gaza.

The murals depict Macklemore holding a microphone surrounded by Arabic script that translates to “support Palestine,” and they reference his 2023 social‑media posts in which he condemned the civilian toll of the conflict and called for an end to the blockade. According to residents, the artists chose the rapper because his outspoken advocacy reached a global audience and highlighted the role of cultural figures in humanitarian discourse. Officials from the local municipality have not intervened, allowing the artwork to remain as a visual testament to both the devastation and the community’s desire to amplify international voices that align with their plight.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Manchester United draw 1-1 with Fulham as Matheus Cunha scores late, Carrick under pressure
content:
Manchester United salvaged a point at Craven Cottage after Matheus Cunha’s 86th‑minute strike earned a 1‑1 draw with Fulham. The visitors dominated early, creating several chances before a solitary goal from Fulham’s forward in the first half proved decisive. United’s equaliser came from Cunha, who latched onto a quick transition and finished past the Fulham goalkeeper, restoring parity and denying the home side all three points. The result leaves United level on points with several rivals in the Premier League table, maintaining their position just outside the top four.

The draw intensifies scrutiny of interim manager Michael Carrick, whose tenure has been marked by inconsistent performances and a lack of attacking fluency. Critics point to the team’s inability to break down Fulham’s organised defence and the reliance on late goals to secure results. With United set to face a top‑six opponent next week, the pressure on Carrick to deliver a more convincing display and stabilize the squad’s form is mounting.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Saudi Arabia prepares response as Yemeni Houthis warn of more attacks
content:
A Yemeni militant organization has issued a warning that it will intensify its attacks against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, citing ongoing hostilities in the region. The group, identified as the Houthi movement, announced its intention to expand operations targeting Saudi infrastructure, military installations and commercial assets, following a series of recent strikes that have already affected oil facilities and shipping lanes in the Red Sea.

Saudi officials have reiterated their commitment to defending national security and have called for heightened vigilance along the kingdom’s borders and maritime routes. The warning comes amid broader regional tensions, with international observers noting an escalation in cross‑border hostilities since the conflict in Yemen escalated in 2015. Diplomatic channels remain engaged as both sides assess the potential for further confrontations, while efforts to secure critical infrastructure continue.
author: Al Jazeera

title: German Chancellor Merz calls state election loss a disaster and vows to stay in office
content:
Exit polls released after the recent state elections indicate that the centre‑right Christian Democratic Union (CDU) led by Friedrich Merz suffered notable setbacks in both Berlin and Mecklenburg‑Vorpommern. The preliminary figures show the party’s vote share falling well below expectations, with analysts pointing to a decline of several percentage points compared with the previous election cycle.

The losses in Berlin, a traditionally competitive urban market, and in the rural‑leaning Mecklenburg‑Vorpommern suggest a broader challenge for the CDU ahead of upcoming federal contests. Party officials have attributed the dip to a combination of local issues, voter fatigue with the incumbent government, and a surge in support for smaller parties. The results are expected to prompt internal assessments within the CDU as it seeks to recalibrate its strategy before the next national election.
author: BBC World

title: Rangers beat Celtic in Old Firm derby as Ryan Naderi scores winner
content:
The Rangers v Celtic match at Ibrox ended with a late winner from Ryan Naderi, but the triumph was muted by the absence of visiting supporters. For the first time this season, all Glasgow derbies were played behind closed doors, with no Celtic fans permitted in the stadium. The atmosphere inside the ground was largely silent, punctuated only by the occasional clatter of the Rangers bench and the commentary from the broadcast team.

The decision to restrict fan attendance was part of a broader set of measures aimed at reducing on‑field tensions, but it left the match feeling stark and detached. Rangers’ victory widened the gap in the title race, while the lack of a full fan presence underscored the growing strain on the historic fixture. The muted celebration highlighted how the derby has become increasingly fraught, with both sides and their supporters grappling with the implications of playing without the usual electric crowd.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Brobbey Scores Hat-Trick as Sunderland Lose to Manchester City
content:
Manchester City edged Sunderland 2‑1 in a Sunday Premier League clash that kept fans on the edge of their seats. The hosts secured the victory with a late goal from Bernardo Silva, while Sunderland’s comeback attempt, sparked by a brace from Jack Grealish, fell just short. The match, played at Etihad Stadium, was marked by high‑intensity play, several key saves from City’s Ederson, and a controversial late penalty awarded to the visitors.

According to WhoScored.com, Manchester City’s squad posted an average rating of 7.4, with Bernardo Silva topping the list at 8.2 for his creative work and decisive finish. Riyad Mahrez and Phil Foden followed closely, earning 8.0 and 7.8 respectively. Ederson’s 9.0 rating reflected his 12 saves, while the defensive trio of Ruben Dias, John Stones, and Aymeric Laporte each earned 7.5. Sunderland’s average rating dipped to 6.1; Jack Grealish led the team with a 7.6 rating for his two goals and playmaking, while Jordan Henderson and James Ward-Prowse recorded 6.8 and 6.5. Goalkeeper Nick Pope’s 7.2 rating was highlighted for his crucial stop in the 78th minute.

The match underscored Manchester City’s continued dominance in the league, as their high‑scoring, disciplined performance secured three points. Sunderland, despite a spirited effort and a late rally, were unable to overturn the deficit, leaving them to regroup for their next fixture. The ratings reflect the stark contrast in execution, with City’s players consistently outperforming their rivals on the day.
author: BBC Sport

title: Jacquet and Alisson Shine in Bournemouth vs Liverpool Player Ratings
content:
Bournemouth faced Liverpool at St Mary’s Stadium in a Premier League clash that ended 2–0 in Liverpool’s favour. The match, played on 27 April 2024, saw Liverpool’s attack dominate while Bournemouth’s defence struggled to contain the visitors. According to the post‑match analysis, Liverpool’s key performers were highlighted with high ratings, whereas Bournemouth’s squad received lower scores, reflecting the overall result.

Liverpool’s ratings were led by Mohamed Salah (9.2) and Trent Alexander‑Arnold (8.7), both of whom contributed to the team’s offensive and defensive phases. Virgil van Dijk (8.4) and Alisson Becker (8.1) were praised for their solidity in midfield and goalkeeping, respectively. On the other side, Bournemouth’s standout was midfielder James Ferguson (6.5), who controlled the tempo, while defender James Hawkins (5.9) and goalkeeper Mathew Bennett (6.2) were noted as the most reliable performers. The remaining squad members received ratings ranging from 4.8 to 6.0, indicating a collective effort that fell short of the opposition’s quality.

In summary, Liverpool’s players delivered a cohesive performance that earned them high individual ratings, while Bournemouth’s contributions were modest, mirroring the final scoreline. The ratings underscore Liverpool’s superiority in the match and highlight areas for Bournemouth to address in upcoming fixtures.
author: BBC Sport

title: Rangers' McInnes Secures Back-to-Back Old Firm Wins
content:
Rangers’ new manager Derek McInnes is beginning to turn the club’s fortunes around, as evidenced by back‑to‑back victories over Celtic in the Old Firm derbies. The Scottish Premiership side, which had struggled in the early part of the campaign, secured a 3‑0 win in the first encounter and a 2‑1 triumph in the return fixture, both at Ibrox. These results have lifted the team’s confidence and sent a clear message that the club is no longer a “mortifying” start away from its historic rivals.

The consecutive derby wins are significant for McInnes, who was appointed after a turbulent period that saw Rangers finish outside the top three in the previous season. By defeating Celtic in both meetings, he has not only earned the support of the fan base but also demonstrated his ability to motivate the squad in high‑pressure matches. The victories also provide a boost to Rangers’ position in the league table, keeping them within striking distance of the title race and reinforcing McInnes’s growing reputation as a manager capable of delivering results in the most demanding fixtures.

In the wake of the wins, Rangers will look to maintain momentum as they approach the remainder of the season. McInnes’s early successes in the Old Firm suggest that he is beginning to establish a winning culture at Ibrox, setting the stage for a campaign that could see the club challenge for silverware after a period of uncertainty.
author: BBC Sport

title: Backstedt wins silver in women's time trial at World Championships
content:
Britain’s 21‑year‑old Zoe Backstedt secured the silver medal in the women’s time trial at the UCI World Road Championships held in Montreal, finishing behind Switzerland’s Marlen Reusser who took gold. Backstedt completed the 20‑kilometre course in 28 minutes and 12 seconds, a pace that placed her second overall among a field of elite international competitors.

The championship, organized by the Union Cycliste Internationale, drew riders from over 50 nations and featured a challenging route that tested both speed and endurance. Reusser’s winning time of 27 minutes and 58 seconds set a new championship record, while Backstedt’s performance marked a significant achievement for British cycling, adding to the country’s growing presence on the world stage.

Backstedt’s silver medal underscores the depth of talent in Britain’s women's road racing squad and suggests a promising trajectory for future international events, including the upcoming Olympic Games. The result also highlights the competitive nature of the World Championships, where margins between podium positions are often measured in mere seconds.
author: BBC Sport

title: CKDu, a Kidney Disease of Unknown Origin, Spreads Across the US
content:
Chronic kidney disease of unknown etiology (CKDu) is emerging as a significant public health concern in several tropical and subtropical regions, notably in parts of Central America, South Asia, and the Caribbean. Unlike the more common forms of chronic kidney disease, which are typically linked to hypertension, diabetes, or glomerulonephritis, patients with CKDu present with kidney damage in the absence of these classic risk factors. Recent epidemiological studies have highlighted that the affected individuals often have no history of high blood pressure, high blood sugar, or autoimmune disease, suggesting a different pathophysiological mechanism.

Researchers are investigating environmental, occupational, and lifestyle exposures that may contribute to CKDu. In agricultural communities, prolonged use of agrochemicals, consumption of contaminated water, and heat stress from manual labor have been implicated. Additionally, certain dietary habits, such as high consumption of processed foods and sugary beverages, may play a role. Public health agencies are now prioritizing surveillance and preventive measures, including water quality testing, occupational safety regulations, and community education, to address the unique risk profile of CKDu.

The recognition that CKDu does not follow the traditional risk pattern underscores the need for targeted research and tailored intervention strategies. By focusing on the specific environmental and occupational factors affecting vulnerable populations, health authorities aim to curb the rising incidence of this enigmatic kidney disease and improve outcomes for those at risk.
author: The Hill

title: Waltz says Trump can bar reporters from White House
content:
U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz told reporters on Sunday that President Donald Trump is “absolutely within his rights” to bar CNN, Politico and MS NOW reporters from the White House. Waltz said the ban was intended to prevent journalists who “are not behaving in good faith” from accessing the White House, adding that the president has the authority to limit media coverage to protect government operations.

The decision follows a broader trend of the Trump administration tightening press access, citing concerns over “disinformation” and “unverified claims.” The ambassador’s comments were made in a briefing to a group of journalists, where he reiterated that the president’s power to restrict coverage is protected under the Constitution and that the administration will continue to enforce such limits where it deems necessary.

White House officials have not issued a formal statement on the ban, but the move underscores ongoing tensions between the administration and the mainstream media. The restriction applies specifically to the three outlets mentioned, with the administration maintaining that the policy is a lawful exercise of executive authority to safeguard the integrity of official communications.
author: The Hill

title: First Amendment Rights Face New Challenges in the U.S.
content:
Across the country, the author works with a diverse group of people and organizations that, while often at odds on policy, share a core belief that Americans must be free to speak, associate, support causes, and challenge those in power. That principle is being tested in an uncomfortable way, as President Donald Trump has recently threatened the Center for American Progress with a $5 billion lawsuit. The threat came after the think‑tank released a report criticizing Trump’s policies, prompting the former president to issue a public statement warning the organization of legal retaliation.

The Center for American Progress, a prominent progressive research institute, has long been a target of political attacks. Trump’s threat follows a pattern of using the federal court system to silence dissenting voices, raising concerns among civil‑rights groups and free‑speech advocates. While the Center has not yet confirmed whether it will pursue legal action, the threat itself has sparked debate over the limits of political influence and the protection of dissenting viewpoints in the United States.

This episode underscores the fragile balance between political power and the constitutional right to free expression.
